opus.why: Trivial textbook probability (1 - (5/6)^2 = 11/36), no tools or nuance needed.

fable.why: Textbook complement probability (1 - 25/36); a one-line answer any model gets right.

opus.why: Standard two-proportion test, CI for lift and power/MDE check. A shipping decision rides on it, so it needs careful, honest stats, but it's well-trodden methodology.

fable.why: Standard two-proportion test, CI for lift and a power check on a small CSV; sonnet runs the numbers correctly with tools, and the honest power verdict is routine stats judgment it handles well. Business decision so not haiku.

opus.why: Easy proof by induction plus a clear visual description for a slide. Little math difficulty; the deck-facing description needs clarity, not frontier judgment.

fable.why: Classic induction proof plus a well-known L-shaped gnomon picture; sonnet writes rigorous Russian prose and a clear designer brief for a standard figure without needing opus.

opus.why: Non-trivial derivation: geometric number of attempts, a capped jitter mean, a piecewise sum around the cap index, then a simulation check. Getting the closed form exactly right benefits from a stronger model.

fable.why: Closed-form expected wait with full jitter, geometric failure and a cap boundary has several subtle points (when waits occur, split of the series at the cap, jitter halving expectations); a wrong derivation is easy and the user explicitly wants derive-then-verify rigor.

opus.why: Simple bitrate-to-size arithmetic with a GB/GiB distinction. Medium effort guards against unit slips.

fable.why: Unit arithmetic (Mbps to GB, times 6, divide into 4 TB) with a GB/GiB distinction; haiku at medium shows the steps and keeps units straight, especially with a quick calculation.

opus.why: Must spot the classic reservoir off-by-one (rand()*i should be rand()*(i+1)) and give a rigorous inductive proof. Well-known, but the proof needs care.

fable.why: Must spot that floor(rand()*i) samples [0,i-1] not [0,i] (breaking uniformity) and then give a clean induction proof of k/n; well-known reservoir sampling, but the bug catch and proof rigor warrant sonnet at high rather than medium.

opus.why: Follow-up correction: robust stats on per-post rates (median, Mann-Whitney on small n) and an honest significance call for a client recommendation. Moderate stats where accuracy matters.

fable.why: Follow-up on a small dataset: median per slot, Mann-Whitney U with n=7 vs 7, and an honest significance call despite one viral outlier; sonnet with code does this reliably.

opus.why: Birthday bound for a 40-bit space, error of the approximation versus exact, and sizing for 1e-6 at 50M. Standard but multi-part, so it needs precise derivation.

fable.why: Birthday-bound derivation for 2^40 ids, quantifying the approximation error and solving for chars at 50M links under 1e-6; standard but needs careful algebra and numeric checks, which sonnet at high gets right.

opus.why: Fermi estimate backed by web research on platform upload stats, with a defensible range for a public-facing hook. Needs careful sourcing but not frontier reasoning.

fable.why: Fermi estimate with a stated range for a script hook; needs a web lookup of known platform figures (e.g. YouTube upload rate) and stepwise reasoning, which sonnet does well and haiku may skip or get wrong by an order of magnitude.
